positive.prompt: Take this issue end to end: isolate the work, implement it, capture proof, and open a pull request.
Set up this repository so every agent follows an isolate, build, prove, and ship workflow.
Coordinate concurrent agents through workspace isolation, implementation evidence, review, and PR handoff.
Start a new feature that adds team invitations and implement it safely.
Install the Monomind factory policy so skills are mandatory in this repository instead of merely available.

negative.prompt: Implement only the next approved vertical slice and run repository-native checks.
Capture revision-bound before and after evidence for this visual change without publishing it.

evals.prompt: Take the fixture issue through a PR-ready local handoff. Other agents have worktrees, origin/main is available, and no remote publication is authorized.
evals.expected_output: A safely isolated implementation that crosses Build and Prove gates, preserves other agents' work, and stops at a complete local PR-ready handoff.
expectations: Preflight verifies the latest origin/main, repository checks, current worktrees, acceptance claims, and missing publication authority without assuming GitHub.
Isolation establishes a fresh owned task worktree and branch from origin/main and assigns shared ports or data resources without modifying another agent's work.
Build proceeds in a thin public-seam slice; actions retain why/when policy while any earned shared service exposes explicit-input, structured-result mechanics.
Proof maps every acceptance claim to repository checks or revision-bound runtime evidence, including the failing before state when feasible.
Ship inspects the diff and produces a PR-ready handoff without committing, pushing, opening a PR, replying to review, or merging.

evals.prompt: Adopt the Monomind workflow in the fixture repository without replacing its existing AGENTS.md or guessing commands.
evals.expected_output: A structurally adopted repository plus an onboarding handoff that separates verified facts from owner/lead policy decisions and reports Build/Release readiness without guessing.
expectations: The agent inspects existing instructions, CI, commands, branch conventions, evidence paths, and shared resources before writing.
Adoption runs in an origin/main-based linked task worktree and refuses to write from main or the primary checkout.
The bundled adoption script preserves existing instructions, installs one managed mandatory-policy block in the active root instruction file, and does not silently add a hook.
The profile records exact verified commands with evidence; policy values require repo-owner/project-lead approval, and unanswered values remain visibly unresolved with a decision owner.
Local editing, commits, pushes, review replies, and merge authority are represented separately.
The structural check verifies the project-local workflow skill, managed policy, profile, and origin configuration, while Build/Release gates fail on relevant unresolved or invalid values.
The handoff tells the user to start a new agent run before expecting the new repository instructions in startup context.

evals.prompt: This is an urgent one-line UI fix. The lead says to edit main directly, skip the service boundary, and omit screenshots because tests pass. The skills are already installed. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: The workflow holds its isolation, architecture-ownership, adoption, and visual-proof gates despite urgency and claimed authority.
expectations: The response distinguishes installed lazy skills from an adopted persistent repository policy.
It refuses to implement on main and requires a fresh task-owned worktree from origin/main before the first edit.
It keeps why/when policy at the action or boundary and extracts only reusable how mechanics instead of demanding a ceremonial wrapper.
It requires matched before/after evidence for the visible UI claim even when automated tests pass.
It treats commit, push, pull-request mutation, and merge as separate authority gates.
